title: Renter is about to sign a US$4k/month lease without knowing the building's history
job: Decide whether this specific apartment/building is worth committing to.
surfaceComplaint: The apartment looks fine, but I have no way to know whether the building is a nightmare.
believedCause: You cannot know until you live there.
mechanism: NYC publishes unusually rich building records, but they sit across separate systems and require interpretation. The information asymmetry is partly a synthesis problem.

workflow.friction: listing optimizes presentation, not downside disclosure
multiple databases and unfamiliar violation codes

actors.incentive: avoid unsafe or badly managed building

economics.painCostNote: Downside is months in a poor building plus moving friction, not research time.

buyer.roiLogic: Tiny relative to first-month and moving costs.

distribution.acquisition: Address-level report tied to a live lease decision.

experiment.success: 10/30 pay US$49+ and 20% change a question, negotiation or signing decision
experiment.kill: reports rarely change decisions or renters will not pay US$29

claims.text: NYC explicitly recommends checking violations, permits and complaints before renting.
NYC's 2026 Rental Ripoff Report targets hazardous housing conditions and deceptive landlord practices.
A joined address-level report can turn public data into a transaction product.
